statement: Every census record of class never or fallback-only is retired: a never site loses its fallback side and, where the primary side can be absent, answers with a named outcome instead of a silent default; a fallback-only site loses its dead primary side and is renamed for what it actually does; each deletion is one attempt per owner directory and cites the census record and run identities that justify it; the budget rows fallback_branches_never_taken and fallback_branches_only_fallback_taken read zero.

constraints.statement: A deletion names the census record (file, hash, class) and the runs behind it. A site whose record is unloaded or whose hash changed since the census is not deletable on census evidence.
Removing a fallback never widens a failure into a crash path: where the primary side can be absent, the result is a typed refusal or named state the consumer handles (R07, R11).
Each attempt changes one owner directory (readiness, partition, raft first) and lands on its own, so a regression is attributable to one owner.
No alias, compatibility branch or parallel implementation is kept for safety; a retained path is a finding routed to its owner, not a preserved fallback.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
